about: BepInEx/config/dev.ptrcraft.cfg in PTR's folder. Settings.cs binds one entry per row (generated).

columns.id: Row id = the C# field name
columns.verified: Evidence from a real run, or 'no'

rows.effect: Replace PTR's player with the Minecraft player while Minecraft is linked
Start the PTRCraft Minecraft (hidden) when PTR starts, unless one is already running
Arguments that start the PTRCraft instance
PTR damage per Minecraft damage point (a biker has about 1.0 health)
PTR damage added to every Minecraft hit (a bare-fist punch = 0.23, about 4 to drop a biker)
Minecraft damage per PTR damage dealt to the player (full PTR health = 10 hearts)
Dying in Minecraft kills PTR's player too: PTR's own death screen and restart (or the end of a Beneath run)
rows.verified: 2026-10-10 01:41 logs: Minecraft 'fell from a high place' -> 'the Minecraft player died' -> PTR's player died and PTR restarted Beneath's Caves floor 1 (epoch 4)

rows.effect: How far Minecraft hits push PTR's people (scenarios, arena, custom levels)
The same in Beneath, whose enemies PTR itself pushes about ten times less (they flew off the map at 1.0)
Minecraft fire (fire, lava, campfires, magma, Fire Aspect, Flame arrows) sets PTR's people burning with PTR's own fire, like the arena's fire traps
Minecraft draws its hand and HUD at most this tall; PTR scales it up
How often Minecraft renders its hand and HUD (PTR's camera never waits)
Hide PTR's health bar, power icons and key prompts while Minecraft's HUD is shown

Minecraft draws its own blocks, mobs, players, arrows, items, particles and your F5 body into the overlay, hidden behind PTR's walls and people; off: PTR draws Minecraft's blocks and entities itself with PTR's lights
